replacements.text: Strongest feature: Craig contests Flew’s material-person premise by identifying diachronic identity, intentionality, and free agency as failures for epiphenomenalism, keeping an unembodied personal cause available. Principal limitation: These challenges reveal explanatory pressure, because they neither compare materialist alternatives nor establish an immaterial self, a bodyless mind’s possibility, or the morally interested God Flew disputes. Live burden: Craig must supply the bridge from mental phenomena to a cosmic agent, while Flew must defend material personhood and explain why gaps support no modal opening. Locked score: The exact 64 follows from logical coherence 62 and evidence warrant 54 for asserted gaps, responsiveness 65 and relevance and burden 67 for partial bridge contact, plus precision and clarity 71 and calibration and charity 72 for an identifiable, limited conclusion.

Strongest feature: Flew exposes the attribute-bridging gap through a counterexample: even a universe-causing being with power or knowledge need not possess moral concern, so a cosmic cause does not entail the standard God-concept. Principal limitation: The objection bundles properties and leans on Genesis framing, insufficiently engaging Craig’s personal-agency inference, cumulative moral case, and resurrection route; it restricts the cosmological conclusion without defeating the case. Live burden: Flew must test bridges individually, while Craig must justify additional attributes and explain why causal, personal, moral, and providential conclusions converge on a being. Locked score: The exact 80 reflects logical coherence 83, evidence warrant 70, responsiveness 86, relevance and burden 82, precision and clarity 79, and calibration and charity 75, rewarding the decisive countermodel while preserving limited scope.
